title: I’m developing L.E.O., a police-versus-contractors FPS with a multiplayer playtest planned for January
author: Snoo_79687
selftext:
I’m developing L.E.O., a first-person shooter featuring 4v4 matches between police and private military contractors.

The next playtest is scheduled for January 2027 and will include all multiplayer modes. I’m using the time before then to polish and improve the build, and the test will help guide further changes ahead of Early Access.

A campaign is planned for the future, but it won’t be included in this playtest. There’s no announced Early Access release date yet. 

I used AI to help with the Bot voices and with promotional artwork.

If it looks like something you’d enjoy, L.E.O. is available to wishlist on Steam. : [https://store.steampowered.com/app/4951460/LEO/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4951460/LEO/)

comments.author: aigamedev-mod
comments.body: u/Snoo_79687 please add details on how AI was used to make this. Just stating that you used AI doesn't pass the rule. The community is a dev community, add dev details. Rule 4 is there to make sure promotional posts contribute by getting into the process and actual development. There's a real risk of the sub being swamped by self-promotion. If you don't update, this post may be removed.

replies.author: Snoo_79687
replies.body:
A bit more detail on how I’ve used AI during development: I used ElevenLabs for the bot voices and my paid ChatGPT account for promotional artwork. I’ve also used AI to help with coding, understanding documentation, and integrating assets in Unreal.

The game’s ideas and direction are my own. There’s been a lot of back-and-forth, explaining what I want and giving specific guidance to get the results where I want them. I’m also putting a lot of attention into keeping the codebase organized, tidy, and reusable as development continues.

One useful part of the workflow has been working with assets from the store. Some of their documentation can be confusing, so I use AI to help break it down, understand how the systems work, and figure out how to modify and connect different assets for my game. That includes help with the code and integration work needed to get those systems working together.

That’s a bigger part of my development process than my original post explained. I’m happy to discuss the workflow and answer questions about it.
